messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a weird drop in Savings Plan utilization for p4d instances in eu-west-1. Dashboard shows ~22% of committed vCPU-hours unused last billing period. Can we do a quick sweep before the renewal window?

liam: ugh, thanks for flagging. Do we know if it's shift in workload (less training) or a provisioning/placement change?

maya: Initial look: model-training jobs decreased (smaller batches) + some instances idled due to node selector mismatch after the kube-scheduler tweak last month. I ran a quick CE query:
```
# Cost Explorer: filter by region/eu-west-1 + instance family p4d
Metrics: UnusedCommitmentHours, UtilizationPercentage
DateRange: 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28
```

eng-cost-bot: Automated alert: SavingsPlan utilization threshold breached in eu-west-1 (p4d) — utilization 78% (threshold 90%). Suggested action: run commitment coverage re-evaluation.

ana: if utilization is 78%, that's around a 22% waste on committed spend. We should not immediately drop coverage — remember committed discounts still beat on-demand for steady baselines. Proposal: reduce SP commit for eu-west-1 p4d by 10% and shift the rest to convertible RIs or on-demand for 3 months while we fix scheduling.

chuck: I worry about burst capacity for peak experiments. Are those peaks still hitting p4d or got moved to other regions? Any cross-region spill?

maya: peaks are still p4d-heavy but about ~60% of peak-hours occur during predictable windows. Cross-region: small spill to us-west-2 for urgent jobs, but not large. If we cut 10% principal, we'd keep canary buffer for peaks.

liam: Another option: we optimize container placement to pack p4d usage into fewer instances and enable continuous batching to reduce vCPU-hours overall. That is a 2–4 week engineering lift. For immediate cost, 10% reduction + short-term on-demand topping seems reasonable.

sre-oncall: Ops note — if you change SP coverage or RI mix, we need to update autoscaler policies and instance placement constraints. Otherwise scaling will auto-provision on-demand in region but might not respect cost intent. I'll own the autoscaler config change.

maya: Action items: 1) liam to run a 7-day packing analysis by 2026-03-10 (owner: liam). 2) ana to draft a savings plan modification request for -10% p4d eu-west-1 with 1-month review (owner: ana, due 2026-03-05). 3) sre-oncall to add autoscaler guardrail change linked to the SP/RI change (owner: sre-oncall, due 2026-03-06). 4) eng-cost-bot: generate a post-change cost projection comparing current vs -10% commit (owner: eng-cost-bot).

eng-cost-bot: Projection task queued — ETA 2 hours. Will post CSV with expected $ savings and break-even.

chuck: thumbs up on that plan. If the packing analysis shows >15% reclaimable via scheduling we can do an additional -5%.

maya: Cool. I'll also add a short eval suite to catch scheduling regressions so we don't bite into utilization again. Thanks folks :thumbsup:

liam: tagging finance for FYI @finance-team — this will change committed spend forecast for Q2.

eng-cost-bot: Note: renewal window for current SP term ends 2026-04-12. Recommend final decision by 2026-03-20 to allow procurement lead time.

maya: Noted. We'll reconvene once the numbers come in.
